meta_title: Vikas Choudhary | Program Manager, FLN & EdTech
meta_desc: Personal website of Vikas Choudhary, Program Manager at Pratham Education Foundation, Maharashtra. Leading 500 ashram schools, a 60-member field team, 48-day FLN catch-up courses, and offline-first AI EdTech.
hero_label: Program Manager · FLN Program Development & EdTech
hero_bio_1: I'm a Program Manager at Pratham Education Foundation with 5+ years in education and the social sector, leading a state-level partnership with the Tribal Development Department (Government of Maharashtra) across 500 tribal residential ashram schools. My work spans everyone from Grade 1 students learning to decode their first word to 29 Project Officers (17 IAS) aligning policy and reporting.
hero_bio_2: Most of what I do is unglamorous: reviewing telemetry data, travelling to remote ashramshalas across Nashik, Thane, Nagpur, and Amravati, troubleshooting implementation failures, and holding honest pedagogical conversations with headmasters and wardens until learning genuinely shifts. I also build practical EdTech, including an offline-first AI student tracking platform and interactive FLN games.
hero_bio_3: Before this I led multi-state STEM programs at Gurushala and American India Foundation, and directed 100+ street plays with Manthan Theatre Foundation. Educated at Kurukshetra University with both a Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) and an M.A. in Hindi Language & Literature with Distinction, a combination of scientific inquiry and linguistic empathy that proves remarkably useful in the field.
currently_text: Leading Majhi Shala, Majha Swabhimaan across 500 Ashram schools in Nashik, Thane, Nagpur, and Amravati. Scaling the 48-Day FLN Catch-Up Course (LSRW + TaRL), implementing a CASEL-based Happiness Curriculum, and deploying an AI-powered offline platform to track child-wise holistic growth.
work_intro: Seven roles across five years: what I've been building, field-testing, and occasionally course-correcting.
work_1_title: Pratham Education Foundation: Majhi Shala, Majha Swabhimaan
work_1_role: Program Manager · Nashik, Thane, Nagpur & Amravati Divisions
work_1_desc_1: Leading the statewide partnership with the Tribal Development Department (Government of Maharashtra) for the holistic development of 500 Ashram schools. I direct a cross-functional field team of 60 across four administrative divisions and serve as primary liaison to 29 Project Officers (17 IAS, 12 Non-IAS) and 29 Assistant Project Officers.
work_1_desc_2: Developed the 48-day FLN Catch-Up Course (TaRL & LSRW) implemented across 500 schools, designed a CASEL-aligned Happiness Curriculum for residential hostels, and vibecoded an AI-powered offline FLN assessment platform with built-in interactive learning games to track student-level growth in low-connectivity zones.
work_2_desc: Led capacity building for 70 School Facilitators across 10 northern states on STEM and Robotics delivery. Liaised with District Primary Education Officers (DPEOs) and DIET principals on techno-pedagogy, and organized state and interstate STEM Expos showcasing student project-based learning.
work_3_role: Assistant Director, Awareness Programs · Theatre Artist
work_3_desc: Directed and performed 100+ street plays (Nukkad Natak) across 25+ villages on public health, child rights, and civic awareness alongside DLSA and local officials. Taught me that authentic communication relies on meeting communities exactly where they are.
work_4_desc: Mobilized 200+ student volunteers for Unnat Bharat Abhiyan surveys, Swachh Bharat internships, and rural literacy outreach. My first real exposure to coordinating people toward a shared goal in conditions where nothing is guaranteed.
writing_intro: Long-form field notes on education, program design, offline EdTech, and what implementation actually looks like. All opinions are my own.
blog_1_title: What 8,575 Assessments Taught Me About Learning Gaps in Tribal Schools
blog_1_excerpt: When our team completed midline assessments across ashram schools in Maharashtra, reading proficiency at the Story level jumped from 14% to 35%. However, the journey to achieve this revealed something far more important than any metric: why honest assessment design matters more than building impressive dashboards.
blog_2_title: Why a Wooden Abacus Still Beats a Spreadsheet in the Classroom
blog_2_excerpt: I've seen plenty of EdTech pitches for tablets and AI tutors. Yet some of my most memorable classroom moments in Amravati and Nashik involved a simple abacus, 3D alphabet letters, and children who couldn't sit still because they were fully engaged in learning.
blog_3_title: The Catch-Up Problem: Reaching Children Who Fell Behind Before We Arrived
blog_3_excerpt: A Class 6 student who cannot read a paragraph hasn't failed; the system moved them along without verifying foundational skills. Scaling remedial education across 500 tribal schools taught me what Catch-Up truly demands of teachers, field teams, and institutions.
thoughts_intro: Shorter reflections on the education and development sector: things I've been thinking about, questioning, or learning.
thought_1_text: "A child who can't read a paragraph by Class 6 isn't a slow learner. They are simply a student that the system moved forward without verifying foundation readiness. The core problem is structural rather than individual."
thought_2_text: "The most powerful teaching tool in a tribal school isn't a digital tablet. It's an educator who believes the child in front of them is capable of learning, backed by the proper skills and materials to make it happen."
thought_3_text: "We frequently discuss data-driven programs, but data is only ever as honest as the actual field conditions that produced it. Prioritize building genuine trust with your field teams first, and accurate numbers will naturally follow."
thought_4_text: "Scale without quality is just organized failure. The BOT model works only when what you're transferring is genuinely owned by the people who will sustain it."
